newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks close virtually flat in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks close virtually flat in dull trade.

text.p: Mexican stocks closed slightly lower Monday in thin volume as traders awaited the outcome of local factors, traders said.

"The market has been almost dead, awaiting domestic developments, like the Bank Debtors' Support programme, the Alliance for Economic Recovery, the government's economic policy guidelines for 1997 and third-quarter earnings reports," a trader said.
The IPC index of blue chip stocks closed down 0.47 of a point, or 0.02 percent, at 3,236.32. Volume was a lifeless 43.1 million shares traded.
Traders said volume was low due to the lack of foreign investors in the market.
"Foreigners have been on the sidelines due to exchange rate fluctuations. The market even ignored movements in Dow industrials today," he added.
Dealers said same-day buy-sell trades in otherwise infrequently traded stocks prevailed again, and at low volume.

An example of this was pharmaceutical stock Nadro, which topped percentage gainers after just 1,000 of its B series shares were traded. Nadro, which had not traded since Sept. 19, gained 2.35 pesos (31 cents) to 25.35 ($3.36).
On the broad market scoreboard, of a total of 109 stocks that changed hands, gainers outnumbered losers by 57 to 30, with the remaining 22 unchanged.
Technical analysts said the IPC's support at 3,200 was holding up to pressure.
"We're testing this level. As long as we don't break it, things won't be so bad," an analyst said.
